newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 21.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 21.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- The fragile multi-party talks in Northern Ireland will face a new crisis on Tuesday as loyalist paramilitaries and their political representatives are accused of duplicity following a booby-trap bomb attack on a Catholic family in County Antrim.
- The former Irish Prime Minister, Charles Haughey, has been admitted to hospital in Dublin for "minor tests".
- Use of a syringe as an offensive weapon is to become an offence under new legislation to be introduced by the Minister for Justice, Nora Owen.
- Boosting the take-home pay of the low paid and making it more attractive to work rather than claim benefit will be one of the main themes of Wednesday's Irish budget.
- The Irish government was given an eve-of-Budget warning on Monday that the economy is overheating due to the biggest rise in consumer spending and house prices for 20 years.
- The Loyalist ceasefire edged nearer to collapse on Monday after terrorists tried to murder a Catholic couple and their five-month-old daughter in a car-bomb attack.
- The Irish pound might have to be formally revalued upwards in the European currency grid if the present strength of the dollar and sterling continues, a leading economist suggested on Monday.
